Faster convolutions with less memory. No API or `.knx` format changes: existing models and code work as before.

## Improvements

**Tiled convolution** (`include/kernix_model.h`)
- im2col and matmul now run tile by tile (2 MB tiles). The unrolled matrix stays in cache instead of making a full round trip through memory.
- Tiles are processed in 4 parallel lanes, so one lane unrolls while another runs its matmul on AMX.
- im2col copies small channel counts with a plain loop instead of `memcpy`, so the first layer of an image model (3 input channels) got about 1.8× faster.

**Shared, bounded im2col buffer**
- All convolutions in a model share one tile-sized im2col buffer. Before, each convolution kept its own full-size buffer.
- The buffer size no longer grows with the batch, and the workspace limit counts it as a fixed cost. With the default 64 MB limit, large batches are no longer split into small chunks unnecessarily.

## Results (Apple M1, ResNet with 32 channels and SE blocks, input 3×32×32, default workspace limit)

| | Batch 1 | Batch 64 | Peak memory (batch 64) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1.0 | 0.60 ms | 41.7 ms | 69.5 MB |
| **v0.1.1** | **0.44 ms** | **20.8 ms** | **40.3 MB** |

- Without a workspace limit, v0.1.0 needed 391 MB at batch 64; v0.1.1 stays at about 40 MB.
- Outputs are unchanged (max relative error 4.5e-7 vs PyTorch).
- Compared with other runtimes (Python calls, same weights):
  - Batch 1: faster than ONNX Runtime CPU, MLX, and PyTorch.
  - Batch 64: on par with PyTorch MPS while using only the CPU and AMX.
  - Core ML is still faster on CNNs because it can use the Neural Engine in float16: 1.9× at batch 1 and 13× at batch 64. See the README limitations.

## Verification

- 17 PyTorch and 21 Keras reference models match the original within 2e-4 relative error (about 1e-7 excluding int8).
- 4,500 corrupted `.knx` files under ASan/UBSan: no memory errors.
- Runtime checks pass on both the Metal and Accelerate builds.

The tile size (2 MB) and lane count (4) were tuned on an M1; other chips may prefer different values.
